input.plan:
# Online Multiplayer for Monecraft

## Context

Monecraft is today a single-player, client-only browser game (Next.js 16 / React 19 / TS strict / Three.js / Bun) saving to localStorage. Goal: online co-op multiplayer played in the browser, with accounts + cloud saves + instant guest access, deployed on managed infrastructure, without breaking offline single-player.

Exploration confirmed the engine is **already a headless simulation core**: `lib/game/engine/` + `lib/world/` (~13.4k LOC) is pure TS (no DOM/WebAudio/rAF), runs under `bun test`, mutates only via `dispatch(Command)` (28-command union in `lib/game/engine/commands.ts`), publishes ~60 `GameEvent`s the renderer/audio already consume as observers, has injectable RNG/Storage, and saves as seed + block diff. The real work is: (a) the state model is single-player-shaped (one `state.player`, ~25 flat per-player fields in `state.ts`); (b) worldgen noise uses `Math.sin` → not portable across JS engines (why CI pins Bun 1.3.12) — a Bun server and a V8 browser can disagree on terrain for the same seed; (c) there is zero server/network code.

### Decisions (confirmed with user)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scale | 2–8 players per world, private co-op via invite link. No chunk streaming / interest management in v1 — full-world rooms. |
| Hosting | **Vercel**: Next.js app, better-auth, world/save/invite API, Neon Postgres. **Fly.io**: one Bun process hosting N world rooms (one `GameEngine` each, ~74 MB/room), WebSocket, 20 Hz fixed tick. They share only Neon + a ticket-signing secret. The game server is a plain Docker container (`/health`, env vars) — portable to Railway/Render/a VPS by swapping deploy config; Cloudflare DO ruled out (128 MB memory cap vs ~74 MB rooms, workerd runtime). |
| Authority | **Server-authoritative with one hybrid concession**: the server runs the real `GameEngine` per room — every gameplay Command (place/break/craft/attack/chest/…) is validated and executed server-side; canonical world state (blocks, mobs, items, chests, time) lives only there. The sole client-owned thing is each player's *own avatar movement* (streamed @20 Hz; server clamps speed/teleports and force-corrects). Full server-auth movement + prediction can be added later without wire changes — `cmd` envelopes already carry seq + claimed pose. |
| Auth | **better-auth**, self-hosted in Next, Postgres-backed, anonymous plugin: guest identity on first online action, in-place upgrade to email/OAuth keeping worlds. Game server never sees cookies — short-lived HS256 join tickets minted by the Next API. |
| SP | Stays fully offline-capable with localStorage saves, same engine (SP = 1-player case), no account required, no network code loaded. Optional cloud sync of SP saves when signed in (gzipped blob, LWW on `updatedAt`). Phase 2's acceptance bar — "entire existing e2e suite passes unchanged" — is the enforcement. |
| Seams | **No "extract the core" phase is needed** — the headless sim already exists and the Bun server imports it directly (Bun runs TS natively, no build step). What we build: Phase 1–2 make it deterministic + multi-player-shaped *in place*; Phase 5 adds the transport seam — `GameSession` (`createLocalSession` = today's offline path; `NetworkSession` = WebSocket + replica engine) with the protocol in shared `lib/net/`. |

## Delivery: 6 phases, each its own `mp/*` branch + PR, verify gate green each time

Phases 1–2 are pure refactors (zero product change) — the risk sponge. 3 (Vercel side) and 4 (Fly side) are independent after 2; 5 needs both.

---

### Phase 1 — Deterministic foundations (`mp/1-deterministic-foundations`)

**Goal:** identical engine source produces byte-identical worlds on Bun and Chromium; engine input surface loses its DOM-isms. No networking, no feel change.

- **Portable worldgen.** New `lib/world/noise.ts`: integer avalanche hash (`Math.imul`/xor-shift) → `hash2D`, integer-lattice value noise (3–4 octaves) replacing `smoothNoise2D`, and `portableSin/Cos` (range-reduce + minimax polynomial) for `carveCaves`' walk and `daylightAt`. Swap into `lib/world/generation.ts`; audit with `grep -nE 'Math\.(sin|cos|tan|atan|exp|log)'` over sim-affecting paths (`playerMotion` trig may stay — frame-local, never seed-determined). **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11** in `lib/game/config.ts`; re-baseline hashes in `lib/world/generation.test.ts` per the documented policy (the structural probes — flat is level, islands flood, villages find flat land — are the acceptance tests for terrain quality). Move digest constants to a new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`.
- **Cross-engine determinism e2e.** New `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`: in-page `crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", engine.state.world.blocks)` vs the baked Bun baseline → proves Chromium ≡ Bun per seed.
- **TickDriver.** New `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`: `createAccumulator` (the exact ≤50 ms/5-substep catch-up lifted from `useMinecraftGame.ts:294-305`) used by the SP rAF loop unchanged, and `createFixedTicker` (drift-corrected chained `setTimeout`, injectable clock) for the phase-4 server. SP stays variable-dt — forcing 20 Hz on the client would add latency for no v1 benefit.
- **Input intents.** `FrameInput` becomes `{ move: {forward,back,left,right,jump,sprint,crouch}, mineHeld }`; `systems/playerMotion.ts:77-91` reads intents; DOM key codes, CapsLock, and pointer-lock resolution move entirely into `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`. `applyLook` unchanged. Shared test helper for the 40+ `FrameInput` call sites.
- **Docs/tests:** architecture.md (input, TickDriver), testing.md (worldgen policy: cross-engine now e2e-pinned; Bun pin no longer load-bearing), save-format.md (v11 worldgen entry — old worlds discard diffs per existing rule), CHANGELOG (flag the world re-roll).

### Phase 2 — Multi-player engine core (`mp/2-multiplayer-engine`) — biggest phase

**Goal:** `players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; all 23 systems converted; save v17; SP behavior and the entire existing e2e suite pass unchanged (the acceptance bar).

- **State** (`state.ts`): `PlayerState` absorbs the ~25 flat per-player fields (position/velocity/yaw/pitch, inventory, armor, selectedSlot, hearts/hunger/oxygen, effects/xp/stats/advancements, isDead/respawnTimer/gameOver, sleeping, spawnPoint, mining, fishing, mountedVehicleId, UI-open flags, `input: FrameInput`, per-player timer split of `GameTimers`). `GameState` gains `players` + `primaryPlayerId`; world timers (spawn directors, randomTick, breed) stay global.
- **Compat aliases** (new `lib/game/engine/players.ts`): `state.player`, `state.inventory`, `state.hearts`, … become accessor properties delegating to the primary player — keeps `window.__monecraft`, every e2e assertion, and shell code working. Permanent, but **engine systems must not use them**: enforce with `no-restricted-syntax` on `state.player` under `lib/game/engine/systems/` once conversion completes.
- **Engine surface** (`GameEngine.ts`): `dispatch(cmd, playerId = primary)`; `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` replaces the `step` input param; `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` (serialize-on-leave); `apiFor(playerId)`; options gain `authority: "local" | "server"` (server ignores `pause`, skips weather + local player motion) and `headless` (skip snapshot building). Player-scoped `GameEvent`s gain `playerId` attribution.
- **Systems** (convert in dependency order, tests green at each step): mobAI targets `nearestTargetablePlayer`; spawn directors round-robin players as spawn centers with a global cap scaled `× ceil(players/2)`; randomTicks split their sample budget across players; **sleep** = per-player `sleeping` flag, fade when *all* non-dead non-spectator players sleep (+ new `wakeUp` command) — SP observable behavior identical; death/respawn per player (SP keeps its "only mobs tick while dead" semantics under `authority:"local"`); hardcore = per-player permadeath→spectator, world `gameOver` when all players are. `ProjectileState.fromPlayer` → `ownerPlayerId`; mob `owner`/vehicle `rider` become PlayerIds.
- **Save v17** (`types.ts`, `save.ts`): world-level fields stay top-level; `players: SavedPlayer[]`; `migrateSaveV16toV17` wraps the flat fields as `[{id:"local", …}]`. Round-trip + migration tests.
- **New tests:** `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (two players: mob targeting, death isolation, inventory isolation, all-asleep night skip, two-player save round-trip). **Docs:** architecture.md engine rewrite, save-format.md v17, testing.md helper, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 3 — Accounts, Postgres, cloud saves, invites (`mp/3-accounts-cloud-saves`)

**Goal:** identity + persistence + ticket mint on the Vercel side. No realtime.

- **DB:** Drizzle ORM + `postgres` driver (runs on both Bun and Node; PGlite driver in tests so CI stays daemon-free). New `db/{schema.ts,index.ts,migrations/}`: better-auth tables (+`skinId`, `isAnonymous`) plus `worlds` (`kind: 'sp-cloud'|'mp'`, seed, worldType, mode/difficulty/hardcore, `saveBlob bytea` gzipped, worldgenVersion, saveVersion, updatedAt), `worldMembers` (role owner|member), `worldInvites` (token, expiry, maxUses).
- **Auth:** `lib/auth/server.ts` (better-auth + anonymous plugin; the account-upgrade hook re-parents worlds/memberships — **integration-test this first**, it's the "guest keeps worlds" promise), `lib/auth/client.ts` (guest session created lazily on first online action, never on plain SP play), `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts`.
- **API routes** (`app/api/`): worlds CRUD; `worlds/[id]/save` GET/PUT gzipped SP blob with 409-on-stale LWW; invites create/resolve/accept; `worlds/[id]/ticket` POST → HS256 JWT (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, Web Crypto, 60 s TTL, claims `{sub, wid, name, skinId, role, pv}`) signed with `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`.
- **Client:** `components/menu/AccountPanel.tsx` (sign in/up, guest, upgrade); `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` (debounced ~60 s push piggybacking the autosave path + on quit; world-select merges local+cloud lists; play downloads blob→localStorage→normal boot; gzip via `CompressionStream`).
- **Dev:** `.env.example` (`DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`), `docker-compose.yml` (postgres:16-alpine).
- **Tests:** ticket round-trip/expiry, PGlite CRUD, invite idempotency, LWW conflict, AccountPanel component tests. **Docs:** new `docs/online.md`, architecture.md web/API layer, CHANGELOG.

**Goal:** Bun room server on Fly speaking protocol v1, persisting to Postgres; fully headless-testable.

- **Shared protocol** `lib/net/protocol.ts` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1`, hand-rolled total validators in `save.ts` house style):
  - C2S: `hello{ticket,protocol}` · `pose{seq,x,y,z,yaw,pitch,onGround}` @20 Hz · `cmd{seq,cmd,pose}` (client-claimed eye pose applied — sanity-checked — before dispatch so aimed raycasts resolve server-side with unchanged `Command` shapes) · `chat` · `ping` · `resync`
  - S2C: `welcome` (ids, seed, mode, roster) · one gzipped binary **world-sync** frame (changes/blockEntities/lootedChests/mobs/vehicles/dayClock) · per-tick `tick{n, ev, pp, mp(10 Hz, deadband), day?, self?}` where `self` is the per-client authoritative delta (inventory/hearts/xp/…) · `mobsKeyframe` every ~5 s · `playerJoined/Left` · `container` · `chat` · `pong` · `forcePose` · `kick{code}`. Close codes 4000–4008. JSON first; envelope leaves room for binary packing later.
  - `lib/net/codec.ts` (gzip: `Bun.gzipSync` / `DecompressionStream`), `lib/net/clock.ts` (RTT EWMA).
- **Server** `server/`: `index.ts` (`Bun.serve`: `/health`, `/rooms` w/ ADMIN_TOKEN, WS upgrade), `roomRegistry.ts`, `room.ts`, `connection.ts` (hello deadline, rate limits), `persistence.ts` (drizzle + in-memory adapter for tests), `remoteMotion.ts` (`applyRemotePoses`: clamp speed to `SPRINT_SPEED×effects×1.25`, reject teleports → `forcePose`, synthesize the move result feeding the unchanged hunger/fall-damage pipeline), `Dockerfile` (`oven/bun:1.3.12` = CI pin), `fly.toml` (single region, health checks, no autostop).
- **Room lifecycle:** construct engine `{authority:"server", headless:true}` from Postgres blob or fresh seed; `createFixedTicker` 20 Hz; persist gzipped save every 60 s + on last-leave + SIGTERM drain; idle 5 min → persist + evict; `MAX_ROOMS` start 6, tuned from `/rooms` p95 tick stats; backpressure via `ws.getBufferedAmount()` (shed pp/mp > 256 KB; kick > 1 MB sustained).

**Goal:** browser plays on the server; SP path untouched.

- **Session seam:** `lib/game/session.ts` — `GameSession { engine, api, kind: "local"|"online" }`; `createLocalSession` absorbs today's construct/save/autosave from `useMinecraftGame.ts` (which now just accepts a session).
- **`lib/net/NetworkSession.ts`:** owns the WS + a **replica engine** (new `replica: true` option: worldgen from seed + join-diff applied, `step` runs only local motion + presentation — mobAI/spawns/dayNight replicated instead). Renderer/audio/minimap/HUD consume the replica's state **unchanged** — no renderer surgery. Outbound: pose @20 Hz; command routing table (local-only: toggles/pause/camera → replica; networked: craft/move/place/attack/… → `cmd` envelope, `selectSlot` optimistic both). Inbound: events replayed onto the replica (block events set `worldMeshDirty`; rest forwarded to the existing renderer/audio event drain); `pp`/`mp` → `lib/net/interpolation.ts` ring buffers sampled at `serverTime − 125 ms`; `self` deltas overwrite replica player fields. Guard the authority/replica system split with a declarative `SYSTEM_SCHEDULE` table (`runsOn: authority|replica|both`) in `GameEngine.step`.
- **Remote avatars:** `lib/game/render/remotePlayerVisuals.ts` reusing `playerModel.ts`/`playerPose.ts` + skin palettes + procedural name-tag sprite.
- **Shell/UX:** world-select **Online** section (create online world, copy invite link); `app/join/[token]/page.tsx` (guest auto-session → accept → play); ticket mint → `NetworkSession.connect`. New `ChatPanel.tsx` (T/Enter, exits pointer lock, fading log; MP-only) and `ConnectionStatus.tsx` (ping badge, reconnect banner, disconnect modal). Pause menu in MP is personal (world keeps running); "Save & Quit" → "Leave world". Mining is server-confirmed (~1 RTT break latency accepted for v1).
- **Tests:** NetworkSession vs fake socket (routing, self-delta, event replay), interpolation math, component tests. **e2e `multiplayer.e2e.ts`:** Playwright boots `next start` + `bun server/index.ts` (`PERSISTENCE=memory`), two browser contexts — B joins A's world via invite, block edit propagates < 2 s, chat round-trips, both see 2 players. **Docs:** manual.md (playing online), online.md, architecture.md session layer, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 6 — Hardening + ops (`mp/6-hardening-ops`) → GA (v0.13.0)

- Reconnect: retry ladder (1/2/4/8 s ×5) with fresh ticket → `resync` → full world-sync + keyframe; e2e kills the socket and asserts seamless resume.
- Latency sim knob: `NetworkSession.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` via `window.__monecraft.net` + env var.
- Replay debugging: per-room ring buffer of `{tick, playerId, cmd}` + pose checkpoints; `/rooms/:id/log` dump; `server/scripts/replay.ts` reproduces server state offline.
- Owner kick + invite revocation; `server/scripts/loadSim.ts` soak (N synthetic clients → tick p95/bandwidth → tune `MAX_ROOMS`, deadbands); `/rooms` stats; runbook in online.md; tuning.md gains net constants.

---

## New dependencies

`better-auth`, `drizzle-orm`, `postgres` (runtime); `drizzle-kit`, `@electric-sql/pglite` (dev). No websocket lib needed (Bun native server, browser native client). Everything else stays procedural/zero-asset.

## Bandwidth/perf sanity (8 players)

S2C ≈ 10–35 KB/s per client JSON (poses 20 Hz, mobs 10 Hz deadbanded, events bursty); join payload ≈ 0.2–1.5 MB gzipped; C2S ≈ 1.2 KB/s. Room tick must stay ≪ 50 ms (SP steps run in single-digit ms today; `/rooms` reports p95 to tune `MAX_ROOMS`).

## Riskiest items (watch list)

1. **Phase 2 blast radius** — contained by the alias layer, dependency-ordered conversion, and the "existing e2e pass unchanged" bar; will dominate the schedule.
2. **better-auth anonymous→upgrade re-parenting** — integration-test before building UI on it.
3. **Value-noise terrain quality** — structural probes pin acceptance; budget a tuning loop.
4. **Single-threaded Bun room budget** — measure, don't assume; scale-out fallback (room→machine affinity via ticket mint) needs no protocol change.
5. Hybrid model trusts client pose on command envelopes (aim/reach hacks possible) — accepted for invite-only co-op; envelope already carries what server-side validation would need later.

## Out of scope for v1

PvP tuning, interest management/chunk streaming, client prediction/rollback, public rooms/matchmaking, moderation, spectator sharing, SP→MP world conversion (schema already permits it later).

## Verification (every phase)

`bun run lint` + `bun run typecheck` + `bun run format:check` + `bun test` + `bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` for phases 1, 2, 5, 6 (renderer/input/shell touched). Manual gameplay pass after phases 1 (terrain look, all four world types) and 5 (two real browsers on a Fly deploy). Docs + tests + CHANGELOG land inside each phase's PR, per AGENTS.md.

# Online Multiplayer for Monecraft

## Context

Monecraft is today a single-player, client-only browser game (Next.js 16 / React 19 / TS strict / Three.js / Bun) saving to localStorage. Goal: online co-op multiplayer played in the browser, with accounts + cloud saves + instant guest access, deployed on managed infrastructure, without breaking offline single-player.

Exploration confirmed the engine is **already a headless simulation core**: `lib/game/engine/` + `lib/world/` (~13.4k LOC) is pure TS (no DOM/WebAudio/rAF), runs under `bun test`, mutates only via `dispatch(Command)` (28-command union in `lib/game/engine/commands.ts`), publishes ~60 `GameEvent`s the renderer/audio already consume as observers, has injectable RNG/Storage, and saves as seed + block diff. The real work is: (a) the state model is single-player-shaped (one `state.player`, ~25 flat per-player fields in `state.ts`); (b) worldgen noise uses `Math.sin` → not portable across JS engines (why CI pins Bun 1.3.12) — a Bun server and a V8 browser can disagree on terrain for the same seed; (c) there is zero server/network code.

### Decisions (confirmed with user)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scale | 2–8 players per world, private co-op via invite link. No chunk streaming / interest management in v1 — full-world rooms. |
| Hosting | **Vercel**: Next.js app, better-auth, world/save/invite API, Neon Postgres. **Fly.io**: one Bun process hosting N world rooms (one `GameEngine` each, ~74 MB/room), WebSocket, 20 Hz fixed tick. They share only Neon + a ticket-signing secret. The game server is a plain Docker container (`/health`, env vars) — portable to Railway/Render/a VPS by swapping deploy config; Cloudflare DO ruled out (128 MB memory cap vs ~74 MB rooms, workerd runtime). |
| Authority | **Server-authoritative with one hybrid concession**: the server runs the real `GameEngine` per room — every gameplay Command (place/break/craft/attack/chest/…) is validated and executed server-side; canonical world state (blocks, mobs, items, chests, time) lives only there. The sole client-owned thing is each player's *own avatar movement* (streamed @20 Hz; server clamps speed/teleports and force-corrects). Full server-auth movement + prediction can be added later without wire changes — `cmd` envelopes already carry seq + claimed pose. |
| Auth | **better-auth**, self-hosted in Next, Postgres-backed, anonymous plugin: guest identity on first online action, in-place upgrade to email/OAuth keeping worlds. Game server never sees cookies — short-lived HS256 join tickets minted by the Next API. |
| SP | Stays fully offline-capable with localStorage saves, same engine (SP = 1-player case), no account required, no network code loaded. Optional cloud sync of SP saves when signed in (gzipped blob, LWW on `updatedAt`). Phase 2's acceptance bar — "entire existing e2e suite passes unchanged" — is the enforcement. |
| Seams | **No "extract the core" phase is needed** — the headless sim already exists and the Bun server imports it directly (Bun runs TS natively, no build step). What we build: Phase 1–2 make it deterministic + multi-player-shaped *in place*; Phase 5 adds the transport seam — `GameSession` (`createLocalSession` = today's offline path; `NetworkSession` = WebSocket + replica engine) with the protocol in shared `lib/net/`. |

## Delivery: 6 phases, each its own `mp/*` branch + PR, verify gate green each time

Phases 1–2 are pure refactors (zero product change) — the risk sponge. 3 (Vercel side) and 4 (Fly side) are independent after 2; 5 needs both.

---

### Phase 1 — Deterministic foundations (`mp/1-deterministic-foundations`)

**Goal:** identical engine source produces byte-identical worlds on Bun and Chromium; engine input surface loses its DOM-isms. No networking, no feel change.

- **Portable worldgen.** New `lib/world/noise.ts`: integer avalanche hash (`Math.imul`/xor-shift) → `hash2D`, integer-lattice value noise (3–4 octaves) replacing `smoothNoise2D`, and `portableSin/Cos` (range-reduce + minimax polynomial) for `carveCaves`' walk and `daylightAt`. Swap into `lib/world/generation.ts`; audit with `grep -nE 'Math\.(sin|cos|tan|atan|exp|log)'` over sim-affecting paths (`playerMotion` trig may stay — frame-local, never seed-determined). **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11** in `lib/game/config.ts`; re-baseline hashes in `lib/world/generation.test.ts` per the documented policy (the structural probes — flat is level, islands flood, villages find flat land — are the acceptance tests for terrain quality). Move digest constants to a new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`.
- **Cross-engine determinism e2e.** New `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`: in-page `crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", engine.state.world.blocks)` vs the baked Bun baseline → proves Chromium ≡ Bun per seed.
- **TickDriver.** New `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`: `createAccumulator` (the exact ≤50 ms/5-substep catch-up lifted from `useMinecraftGame.ts:294-305`) used by the SP rAF loop unchanged, and `createFixedTicker` (drift-corrected chained `setTimeout`, injectable clock) for the phase-4 server. SP stays variable-dt — forcing 20 Hz on the client would add latency for no v1 benefit.

- **Save v17** (`types.ts`, `save.ts`): world-level fields stay top-level; `players: SavedPlayer[]`; `migrateSaveV16toV17` wraps the flat fields as `[{id:"local", …}]`. Round-trip + migration tests.
- **New tests:** `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (two players: mob targeting, death isolation, inventory isolation, all-asleep night skip, two-player save round-trip). **Docs:** architecture.md engine rewrite, save-format.md v17, testing.md helper, CHANGELOG.

- **Tests:** ticket round-trip/expiry, PGlite CRUD, invite idempotency, LWW conflict, AccountPanel component tests. **Docs:** new `docs/online.md`, architecture.md web/API layer, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 4 — Game server + protocol (`mp/4-game-server-protocol`)

**Goal:** Bun room server on Fly speaking protocol v1, persisting to Postgres; fully headless-testable.

- **Shared protocol** `lib/net/protocol.ts` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1`, hand-rolled total validators in `save.ts` house style):

# Online Multiplayer for Monecraft

## Context

Monecraft is today a single-player, client-only browser game (Next.js 16 / React 19 / TS strict / Three.js / Bun) saving to localStorage. Goal: online co-op multiplayer played in the browser, with accounts + cloud saves + instant guest access, deployed on managed infrastructure, without breaking offline single-player.

Exploration confirmed the engine is **already a headless simulation core**: `lib/game/engine/` + `lib/world/` (~13.4k LOC) is pure TS (no DOM/WebAudio/rAF), runs under `bun test`, mutates only via `dispatch(Command)` (28-command union in `lib/game/engine/commands.ts`), publishes ~60 `GameEvent`s the renderer/audio already consume as observers, has injectable RNG/Storage, and saves as seed + block diff. The real work is: (a) the state model is single-player-shaped (one `state.player`, ~25 flat per-player fields in `state.ts`); (b) worldgen noise uses `Math.sin` → not portable across JS engines (why CI pins Bun 1.3.12) — a Bun server and a V8 browser can disagree on terrain for the same seed; (c) there is zero server/network code.

### Decisions (confirmed with user)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scale | 2–8 players per world, private co-op via invite link. No chunk streaming / interest management in v1 — full-world rooms. |
| Hosting | **Vercel**: Next.js app, better-auth, world/save/invite API, Neon Postgres. **Fly.io**: one Bun process hosting N world rooms (one `GameEngine` each, ~74 MB/room), WebSocket, 20 Hz fixed tick. They share only Neon + a ticket-signing secret. The game server is a plain Docker container (`/health`, env vars) — portable to Railway/Render/a VPS by swapping deploy config; Cloudflare DO ruled out (128 MB memory cap vs ~74 MB rooms, workerd runtime). |
| Authority | **Server-authoritative with one hybrid concession**: the server runs the real `GameEngine` per room — every gameplay Command (place/break/craft/attack/chest/…) is validated and executed server-side; canonical world state (blocks, mobs, items, chests, time) lives only there. The sole client-owned thing is each player's *own avatar movement* (streamed @20 Hz; server clamps speed/teleports and force-corrects). Full server-auth movement + prediction can be added later without wire changes — `cmd` envelopes already carry seq + claimed pose. |
| Auth | **better-auth**, self-hosted in Next, Postgres-backed, anonymous plugin: guest identity on first online action, in-place upgrade to email/OAuth keeping worlds. Game server never sees cookies — short-lived HS256 join tickets minted by the Next API. |
| SP | Stays fully offline-capable with localStorage saves, same engine (SP = 1-player case), no account required, no network code loaded. Optional cloud sync of SP saves when signed in (gzipped blob, LWW on `updatedAt`). Phase 2's acceptance bar — "entire existing e2e suite passes unchanged" — is the enforcement. |
| Seams | **No "extract the core" phase is needed** — the headless sim already exists and the Bun server imports it directly (Bun runs TS natively, no build step). What we build: Phase 1–2 make it deterministic + multi-player-shaped *in place*; Phase 5 adds the transport seam — `GameSession` (`createLocalSession` = today's offline path; `NetworkSession` = WebSocket + replica engine) with the protocol in shared `lib/net/`. |

The real work is: (a) the state model is single-player-shaped (one `state.player`, ~25 flat per-player fields in `state.ts`); (b) worldgen noise uses `Math.sin` → not portable across JS engines (why CI pins Bun 1.3.12) — a Bun server and a V8 browser can disagree on terrain for the same seed; (c) there is zero server/network code.

### Decisions (confirmed with user)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scale | 2–8 players per world, private co-op via invite link. No chunk streaming / interest management in v1 — full-world rooms. |
| Hosting | **Vercel**: Next.js app, better-auth, world/save/invite API, Neon Postgres. **Fly.io**: one Bun process hosting N world rooms (one `GameEngine` each, ~74 MB/room), WebSocket, 20 Hz fixed tick. They share only Neon + a ticket-signing secret. The game server is a plain Docker container (`/health`, env vars) — portable to Railway/Render/a VPS by swapping deploy config; Cloudflare DO ruled out (128 MB memory cap vs ~74 MB rooms, workerd runtime). |
| Authority | **Server-authoritative with one hybrid concession**: the server runs the real `GameEngine` per room — every gameplay Command (place/break/craft/attack/chest/…) is validated and executed server-side; canonical world state (blocks, mobs, items, chests, time) lives only there. The sole client-owned thing is each player's *own avatar movement* (streamed @20 Hz; server clamps speed/teleports and force-corrects). Full server-auth movement + prediction can be added later without wire changes — `cmd` envelopes already carry seq + claimed pose. |
| Auth | **better-auth**, self-hosted in Next, Postgres-backed, anonymous plugin: guest identity on first online action, in-place upgrade to email/OAuth keeping worlds. Game server never sees cookies — short-lived HS256 join tickets minted by the Next API. |
| SP | Stays fully offline-capable with localStorage saves, same engine (SP = 1-player case), no account required, no network code loaded. Optional cloud sync of SP saves when signed in (gzipped blob, LWW on `updatedAt`). Phase 2's acceptance bar — "entire existing e2e suite passes unchanged" — is the enforcement. |
| Seams | **No "extract the core" phase is needed** — the headless sim already exists and the Bun server imports it directly (Bun runs TS natively, no build step). What we build: Phase 1–2 make it deterministic + multi-player-shaped *in place*; Phase 5 adds the transport seam — `GameSession` (`createLocalSession` = today's offline path; `NetworkSession` = WebSocket + replica engine) with the protocol in shared `lib/net/`. |

## Delivery: 6 phases, each its own `mp/*` branch + PR, verify gate green each time

Phases 1–2 are pure refactors (zero product change) — the risk sponge. 3 (Vercel side) and 4 (Fly side) are independent after 2; 5 needs both.

---

### Phase 1 — Deterministic foundations (`mp/1-deterministic-foundations`)

**Goal:** identical engine source produces byte-identical worlds on Bun and Chromium; engine input surface loses its DOM-isms. No networking, no feel change.

- **Portable worldgen.** New `lib/world/noise.ts`: integer avalanche hash (`Math.imul`/xor-shift) → `hash2D`, integer-lattice value noise (3–4 octaves) replacing `smoothNoise2D`, and `portableSin/Cos` (range-reduce + minimax polynomial) for `carveCaves`' walk and `daylightAt`. Swap into `lib/world/generation.ts`; audit with `grep -nE 'Math\.(sin|cos|tan|atan|exp|log)'` over sim-affecting paths (`playerMotion` trig may stay — frame-local, never seed-determined). **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11** in `lib/game/config.ts`; re-baseline hashes in `lib/world/generation.test.ts` per the documented policy (the structural probes — flat is level, islands flood, villages find flat land — are the acceptance tests for terrain quality). Move digest constants to a new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`.
- **Cross-engine determinism e2e.** New `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`: in-page `crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", engine.state.world.blocks)` vs the baked Bun baseline → proves Chromium ≡ Bun per seed.
- **TickDriver.** New `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`: `createAccumulator` (the exact ≤50 ms/5-substep catch-up lifted from `useMinecraftGame.ts:294-305`) used by the SP rAF loop unchanged, and `createFixedTicker` (drift-corrected chained `setTimeout`, injectable clock) for the phase-4 server. SP stays variable-dt — forcing 20 Hz on the client would add latency for no v1 benefit.
- **Input intents.** `FrameInput` becomes `{ move: {forward,back,left,right,jump,sprint,crouch}, mineHeld }`; `systems/playerMotion.ts:77-91` reads intents; DOM key codes, CapsLock, and pointer-lock resolution move entirely into `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`. `applyLook` unchanged. Shared test helper for the 40+ `FrameInput` call sites.
- **Docs/tests:** architecture.md (input, TickDriver), testing.md (worldgen policy: cross-engine now e2e-pinned; Bun pin no longer load-bearing), save-format.md (v11 worldgen entry — old worlds discard diffs per existing rule), CHANGELOG (flag the world re-roll).

### Phase 2 — Multi-player engine core (`mp/2-multiplayer-engine`) — biggest phase

**Goal:** `players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; all 23 systems converted; save v17; SP behavior and the entire existing e2e suite pass unchanged (the acceptance bar).

- **State** (`state.ts`): `PlayerState` absorbs the ~25 flat per-player fields (position/velocity/yaw/pitch, inventory, armor, selectedSlot, hearts/hunger/oxygen, effects/xp/stats/advancements, isDead/respawnTimer/gameOver, sleeping, spawnPoint, mining, fishing, mountedVehicleId, UI-open flags, `input: FrameInput`, per-player timer split of `GameTimers`). `GameState` gains `players` + `primaryPlayerId`; world timers (spawn directors, randomTick, breed) stay global.
- **Compat aliases** (new `lib/game/engine/players.ts`): `state.player`, `state.inventory`, `state.hearts`, … become accessor properties delegating to the primary player — keeps `window.__monecraft`, every e2e assertion, and shell code working. Permanent, but **engine systems must not use them**: enforce with `no-restricted-syntax` on `state.player` under `lib/game/engine/systems/` once conversion completes.
- **Engine surface** (`GameEngine.ts`): `dispatch(cmd, playerId = primary)`; `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` replaces the `step` input param; `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` (serialize-on-leave); `apiFor(playerId)`; options gain `authority: "local" | "server"` (server ignores `pause`, skips weather + local player motion) and `headless` (skip snapshot building). Player-scoped `GameEvent`s gain `playerId` attribution.
- **Systems** (convert in dependency order, tests green at each step): mobAI targets `nearestTargetablePlayer`; spawn directors round-robin players as spawn centers with a global cap scaled `× ceil(players/2)`; randomTicks split their sample budget across players; **sleep** = per-player `sleeping` flag, fade when *all* non-dead non-spectator players sleep (+ new `wakeUp` command) — SP observable behavior identical; death/respawn per player (SP keeps its "only mobs tick while dead" semantics under `authority:"local"`); hardcore = per-player permadeath→spectator, world `gameOver` when all players are. `ProjectileState.fromPlayer` → `ownerPlayerId`; mob `owner`/vehicle `rider` become PlayerIds.
- **Save v17** (`types.ts`, `save.ts`): world-level fields stay top-level; `players: SavedPlayer[]`; `migrateSaveV16toV17` wraps the flat fields as `[{id:"local", …}]`. Round-trip + migration tests.
- **New tests:** `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (two players: mob targeting, death isolation, inventory isolation, all-asleep night skip, two-player save round-trip). **Docs:** architecture.md engine rewrite, save-format.md v17, testing.md helper, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 3 — Accounts, Postgres, cloud saves, invites (`mp/3-accounts-cloud-saves`)

**Goal:** identity + persistence + ticket mint on the Vercel side. No realtime.

- **DB:** Drizzle ORM + `postgres` driver (runs on both Bun and Node; PGlite driver in tests so CI stays daemon-free). New `db/{schema.ts,index.ts,migrations/}`: better-auth tables (+`skinId`, `isAnonymous`) plus `worlds` (`kind: 'sp-cloud'|'mp'`, seed, worldType, mode/difficulty/hardcore, `saveBlob bytea` gzipped, worldgenVersion, saveVersion, updatedAt), `worldMembers` (role owner|member), `worldInvites` (token, expiry, maxUses).
- **Auth:** `lib/auth/server.ts` (better-auth + anonymous plugin; the account-upgrade hook re-parents worlds/memberships — **integration-test this first**, it's the "guest keeps worlds" promise), `lib/auth/client.ts` (guest session created lazily on first online action, never on plain SP play), `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts`.
- **API routes** (`app/api/`): worlds CRUD; `worlds/[id]/save` GET/PUT gzipped SP blob with 409-on-stale LWW; invites create/resolve/accept; `worlds/[id]/ticket` POST → HS256 JWT (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, Web Crypto, 60 s TTL, claims `{sub, wid, name, skinId, role, pv}`) signed with `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`.
- **Client:** `components/menu/AccountPanel.tsx` (sign in/up, guest, upgrade); `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` (debounced ~60 s push piggybacking the autosave path + on quit; world-select merges local+cloud lists; play downloads blob→localStorage→normal boot; gzip via `CompressionStream`).
- **Dev:** `.env.example` (`DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`), `docker-compose.yml` (postgres:16-alpine).
- **Tests:** ticket round-trip/expiry, PGlite CRUD, invite idempotency, LWW conflict, AccountPanel component tests. **Docs:** new `docs/online.md`, architecture.md web/API layer, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 4 — Game server + protocol (`mp/4-game-server-protocol`)

**Goal:** Bun room server on Fly speaking protocol v1, persisting to Postgres; fully headless-testable.

- **Shared protocol** `lib/net/protocol.ts` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1`, hand-rolled total validators in `save.ts` house style):
  - C2S: `hello{ticket,protocol}` · `pose{seq,x,y,z,yaw,pitch,onGround}` @20 Hz · `cmd{seq,cmd,pose}` (client-claimed eye pose applied — sanity-checked — before dispatch so aimed raycasts resolve server-side with unchanged `Command` shapes) · `chat` · `ping` · `resync`
  - S2C: `welcome` (ids, seed, mode, roster) · one gzipped binary **world-sync** frame (changes/blockEntities/lootedChests/mobs/vehicles/dayClock) · per-tick `tick{n, ev, pp, mp(10 Hz, deadband), day?, self?}` where `self` is the per-client authoritative delta (inventory/hearts/xp/…) · `mobsKeyframe` every ~5 s · `playerJoined/Left` · `container` · `chat` · `pong` · `forcePose` · `kick{code}`. Close codes 4000–4008. JSON first; envelope leaves room for binary packing later.
  - `lib/net/codec.ts` (gzip: `Bun.gzipSync` / `DecompressionStream`), `lib/net/clock.ts` (RTT EWMA).
- **Server** `server/`: `index.ts` (`Bun.serve`: `/health`, `/rooms` w/ ADMIN_TOKEN, WS upgrade), `roomRegistry.ts`, `room.ts`, `connection.ts` (hello deadline, rate limits), `persistence.ts` (drizzle + in-memory adapter for tests), `remoteMotion.ts` (`applyRemotePoses`: clamp speed to `SPRINT_SPEED×effects×1.25`, reject teleports → `forcePose`, synthesize the move result feeding the unchanged hunger/fall-damage pipeline), `Dockerfile` (`oven/bun:1.3.12` = CI pin), `fly.toml` (single region, health checks, no autostop).
- **Room lifecycle:** construct engine `{authority:"server", headless:true}` from Postgres blob or fresh seed; `createFixedTicker` 20 Hz; persist gzipped save every 60 s + on last-leave + SIGTERM drain; idle 5 min → persist + evict; `MAX_ROOMS` start 6, tuned from `/rooms` p95 tick stats; backpressure via `ws.getBufferedAmount()` (shed pp/mp > 256 KB; kick > 1 MB sustained).
- **No build step:** Bun honors root tsconfig `paths` natively — `bun server/index.ts` just runs; `tsc --noEmit` already covers it; ESLint `no-restricted-imports` keeps `server/**` out of render/audio/ui/components.
- **Tests:** protocol validators, fixed-ticker drift (fake clock), `room.test.ts` with fake sockets + in-memory persistence (join/edit propagation/speedhack correction/idle eviction/self-deltas), one real-socket smoke on an ephemeral port; `scripts/netProbe.ts` CLI client for staging. **Docs:** new `docs/protocol.md`, online.md ops section, architecture.md server layer, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 5 — Client online play (`mp/5-client-online-play`)

**Goal:** browser plays on the server; SP path untouched.

- **Session seam:** `lib/game/session.ts` — `GameSession { engine, api, kind: "local"|"online" }`; `createLocalSession` absorbs today's construct/save/autosave from `useMinecraftGame.ts` (which now just accepts a session).
- **`lib/net/NetworkSession.ts`:** owns the WS + a **replica engine** (new `replica: true` option: worldgen from seed + join-diff applied, `step` runs only local motion + presentation — mobAI/spawns/dayNight replicated instead). Renderer/audio/minimap/HUD consume the replica's state **unchanged** — no renderer surgery. Outbound: pose @20 Hz; command routing table (local-only: toggles/pause/camera → replica; networked: craft/move/place/attack/… → `cmd` envelope, `selectSlot` optimistic both). Inbound: events replayed onto the replica (block events set `worldMeshDirty`; rest forwarded to the existing renderer/audio event drain); `pp`/`mp` → `lib/net/interpolation.ts` ring buffers sampled at `serverTime − 125 ms`; `self` deltas overwrite replica player fields. Guard the authority/replica system split with a declarative `SYSTEM_SCHEDULE` table (`runsOn: authority|replica|both`) in `GameEngine.step`.
- **Remote avatars:** `lib/game/render/remotePlayerVisuals.ts` reusing `playerModel.ts`/`playerPose.ts` + skin palettes + procedural name-tag sprite.
- **Shell/UX:** world-select **Online** section (create online world, copy invite link); `app/join/[token]/page.tsx` (guest auto-session → accept → play); ticket mint → `NetworkSession.connect`. New `ChatPanel.tsx` (T/Enter, exits pointer lock, fading log; MP-only) and `ConnectionStatus.tsx` (ping badge, reconnect banner, disconnect modal). Pause menu in MP is personal (world keeps running); "Save & Quit" → "Leave world". Mining is server-confirmed (~1 RTT break latency accepted for v1).
- **Tests:** NetworkSession vs fake socket (routing, self-delta, event replay), interpolation math, component tests. **e2e `multiplayer.e2e.ts`:** Playwright boots `next start` + `bun server/index.ts` (`PERSISTENCE=memory`), two browser contexts — B joins A's world via invite, block edit propagates < 2 s, chat round-trips, both see 2 players. **Docs:** manual.md (playing online), online.md, architecture.md session layer, CHANGELOG.

### Phase 6 — Hardening + ops (`mp/6-hardening-ops`) → GA (v0.13.0)

- Reconnect: retry ladder (1/2/4/8 s ×5) with fresh ticket → `resync` → full world-sync + keyframe; e2e kills the socket and asserts seamless resume.
- Latency sim knob: `NetworkSession.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` via `window.__monecraft.net` + env var.
- Replay debugging: per-room ring buffer of `{tick, playerId, cmd}` + pose checkpoints; `/rooms/:id/log` dump; `server/scripts/replay.ts` reproduces server state offline.
- Owner kick + invite revocation; `server/scripts/loadSim.ts` soak (N synthetic clients → tick p95/bandwidth → tune `MAX_ROOMS`, deadbands); `/rooms` stats; runbook in online.md; tuning.md gains net constants.

---

## Local development & play

- **Single-player (unchanged):** `bun run dev` → http://localhost:3000 → play offline exactly as today. No Postgres, no game server, no account — SP never touches the network stack.
- **Full online stack on localhost:** `docker compose up -d` (Postgres) + `bun run dev` (Next: menus, auth, API) + `bun server/index.ts` (game server, ws://localhost:8080). A `bun run dev:all` script starts all three; `.env.example` documents the env vars. Open two browser windows, sign in as two guests, join the same world via the invite link — full multiplayer against yourself on localhost.
- **Quick server-only iteration:** the game server runs with `PERSISTENCE=memory` (no DB) — same mode the Playwright MP e2e uses; `scripts/netProbe.ts` connects a CLI client for protocol debugging without a browser.
- **Debugging:** `window.__monecraft` handle keeps working in SP and MP (replica engine); Phase 6 adds a latency-simulation knob (`window.__monecraft.net.setSimulatedLatency(ms)`) and server-side command-log capture + offline replay (`server/scripts/replay.ts`).

## New dependencies

`better-auth`, `drizzle-orm`, `postgres` (runtime); `drizzle-kit`, `@electric-sql/pglite` (dev). No websocket lib needed (Bun native server, browser native client). Everything else stays procedural/zero-asset.

## Bandwidth/perf sanity (8 players)

S2C ≈ 10–35 KB/s per client JSON (poses 20 Hz, mobs 10 Hz deadbanded, events bursty); join payload ≈ 0.2–1.5 MB gzipped; C2S ≈ 1.2 KB/s. Room tick must stay ≪ 50 ms (SP steps run in single-digit ms today; `/rooms` reports p95 to tune `MAX_ROOMS`).

## Riskiest items (watch list)

1. **Phase 2 blast radius** — contained by the alias layer, dependency-ordered conversion, and the "existing e2e pass unchanged" bar; will dominate the schedule.
2. **better-auth anonymous→upgrade re-parenting** — integration-test before building UI on it.
3. **Value-noise terrain quality** — structural probes pin acceptance; budget a tuning loop.
4. **Single-threaded Bun room budget** — measure, don't assume; scale-out fallback (room→machine affinity via ticket mint) needs no protocol change.
5. Hybrid model trusts client pose on command envelopes (aim/reach hacks possible) — accepted for invite-only co-op; envelope already carries what server-side validation would need later.

## Out of scope for v1

PvP tuning, interest management/chunk streaming, client prediction/rollback, public rooms/matchmaking, moderation, spectator sharing, SP→MP world conversion (schema already permits it later).

## Verification (every phase)

`bun run lint` + `bun run typecheck` + `bun run format:check` + `bun test` + `bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` for phases 1, 2, 5, 6 (renderer/input/shell touched). Manual gameplay pass after phases 1 (terrain look, all four world types) and 5 (two real browsers on a Fly deploy). Docs + tests + CHANGELOG land inside each phase's PR, per AGENTS.md.

74:2. A **Bun version bump** — the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined (ECMA-262 leaves transcendentals implementation-specific). 78:The **deep-cave lava worldgen** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. 80:The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was the prior re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.

23:- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of **worldgen** loot chests (dungeon, shipwreck, or buried treasure) the player has already opened or broken. Worldgen chests' contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`, mixed with a per-family constant, from the family's own table) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only sets of _which_ indices belong to each family are not stored; they are re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` / `collectShipwreckSites` / `collectTreasureSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). The field kept its name when shipwrecks/buried treasure generalized it (state-side it is `lootedWorldgenChests`), so pre-aquatic saves read unchanged. Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
43:- **Unreleased (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10)** — the **aquatic update**. Kelp/coral (`BlockId`s **appended**: 55–57), sunken **shipwrecks**, and **buried treasure** all write generated blocks, so the worldgen baseline bumps 9→10 (old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed; the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md). The save **schema stays v16**: cod/salmon are fungible wild mobs (never persisted; `restoreMobs` in older builds drops unknown kinds), kelp growth/harvest rides the block diff, the `treasure_map`/`dried_kelp`/coral items are additive string ids with **no instance state** (the map's compass target is derived from the seed at runtime), and shipwreck/buried chests reuse the persisted `lootedChests` index set unchanged (see above — the fill family is re-derived, not stored).
44:- **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.
45:- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). Validated against the known professions on load. **Generated villages** in the same release bump **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** (villages add structures, so old block-diffs are stale and discarded — the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md); village residents persist via the existing v14 `mobs` field, and **raids** are transient (`state.raid` + raiders aren't serialized, like the boss), so neither needs further save schema beyond the additive `profession` and the by-id Ominous Horn item.
46:- **v14** (persisted mobs — Living World, PR 1) — adds an optional top-level `mobs` (`SavedMob[]`). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no persisted mobs; the world re-seeds its wildlife as before). This is the first mob persistence in the format: `isPersistentMob` keeps only **tamed pets** here (PR-B adds village residents), since the fungible population is re-created each boot. Restored before `spawnInitialMobs`, with `y` re-grounded onto the current surface and fresh ids assigned. The new `faction`/`owner`/`sitting`/`targetId`/`retargetTimer` mob fields are session-side; only the durable ones land in `SavedMob`. The wolf and cat are additive `MobKind`s with no `BlockId`/item changes, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
47:- **v13** (advancements & statistics) — adds optional top-level `stats` (`{ id, value }[]`) and `advancements` (`string[]`). `migrateSaveV12toV13` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ no stats, no advancements yet earned). Both are progression meta folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint and, like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` and `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. No new `BlockId`, no new item, and no worldgen change — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
48:- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
49:- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
50:- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
51:- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

63	**Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.
64	
65	## The worldgen hash policy
66	
67	Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.
68	
69	**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**
70	
71	Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly two cases:
72	
73	1. A **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.
74	2. A **Bun version bump** — the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined (ECMA-262 leaves transcendentals implementation-specific). CI pins `bun-version` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for this reason; bump both together and verify the digests merely shifted rather than the generation logic changing.
75	
76	To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values in the same commit as the cause.
77	
78	The **deep-cave lava worldgen** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. **Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. ## The worldgen hash policy

Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.12.0] - 2026-07-03

### Added

- **The aquatic update**: the ocean the new rafts and ships sail is now worth sailing — fish, flora, wrecks to dive, and treasure to hunt, all on **zero binary assets**. Bumps **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10** (kelp/coral/wrecks/buried chests write generated blocks, so existing worlds reboot from their seed and every worldgen/world-type/meshing digest except flat was re-baselined per docs/testing.md) with **no save-schema change** — the schema stays **v16**.
  - **Kelp & coral**: the sandy ocean floor grows swaying **kelp stalks** and pink/blue **reef coral** (a new hash-gated `placeOceanFlora` pass that consumes no shared PRNG). Kelp is a solid cube painted to read as a plant (the wheat trick — no new geometry): stalks always keep a **3-block clear-water band** below the surface so boats and fishing casts never snag, growth via the existing random-tick sampler enforces the same cap, and **breaking a cell breaks the stalk above it, refilling submerged cells with water — never air**. Kelp smelts **3-at-a-time into dried kelp** (a 2-hunger snack); corals are decorative salvage. New `BlockId`s **appended** (55–57)
  - **Cod & salmon**: the first water-dwelling mobs. A dedicated **aquatic AI branch** (3D wander/flee, every move gated on the destination cell being water, no ground clamp) runs before any land logic; a beached fish flops and suffocates. Both drop **raw fish** — the recipe-book hint for it now reads "Hunt a cod". Fish are fungible (never persisted; old saves load cleanly), spawn as schools in whatever water lies near spawn, and a new **aquatic spawn director** trickles them in around the player (up to `AQUATIC_CAP` 24) so far-flung oceans are stocked too — failing closed on dry worlds (Superflat spawns none). Legless "fish" model variant on `createMobModel`, bubble-blip ZZFX calls
  - **Shipwrecks**: flooded plank hulls (broken walls, snapped mast, always fully submerged) sink onto the deep ocean floor on their own decoupled PRNG, holding 1–2 chests of nautical salvage — and the **treasure map** at a 40% roll. The dungeon lazy-fill generalizes to `fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted`: the site set holding a chest's index picks both the loot table and a family-distinct seed constant, and **all families share the persisted `lootedChests` field unchanged** (no re-roll exploit, no save bump)
  - **Buried treasure & the treasure map**: hold a map (wreck loot, or a rare fishing catch) and a **compass pill** points at the _nearest_ unearthed hoard while red **X**s mark the minimap; dig two blocks under the beach sand for the richest chest table in the game (emeralds guaranteed). The map is deliberately **stateless** — no per-item target, no save field: the compass derives everything from the seed and retargets automatically after each dig. Chests place on a fourth decoupled PRNG with a **seed-pure beach proxy** (terrain-height band + a below-sea neighbor column — never post-water block reads), sand-capped so a breaching cave can't expose them. First dig fires the new **treasureUnearthed** event → **X Marks the Spot** advancement + a **Treasures Unearthed** statistic
---
26:- UI pixel art is procedural: `lib/ui/` generates 16×16 item/HUD sprites as pure pixel buffers (`spritePixels.ts`, `hudPixels.ts` — DOM-free, unit-tested) wrapped by a cached canvas→data-URL layer (`sprites.ts`, falls back to a transparent pixel under happy-dom). `chromeTiles.ts` (`installUiTiles`, idempotent, `document`-guarded) installs the GUI textures as CSS vars: the menu-backdrop noise (`--mc-tile-dirt/stone`) and the chrome grain layered over the flat panel/slot/button colors (`--mc-tile-panel/well/button`, which default to `none` so SSR/pre-install falls back to the solid color). No image assets, no licensing exposure. `lib/ui/` must not import Three.js or the engine.
78:**Dungeon loot chests.** Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents can't ride the block-diff baseline. The engine instead keeps two session-only sets — `dungeonChestIndices` / `dungeonSpawnerIndices` — rebuilt each boot from the seed via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`, which replays the dungeon placement math without writing blocks), plus a **persisted** `lootedDungeonChests` set. On a dungeon chest's first open or break, `systems/dungeon.ts` `fillDungeonChestIfUnlooted` rolls loot seeded from `world.seed ^ voxelIndex` (`lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`) and marks the index looted. Gating on the looted set — not on whether the chest is currently non-empty — is what stops an emptied-then-reloaded chest from re-rolling (an empty container is dropped from `blockEntities`).
93:- **Atmosphere** (all procedural, zero assets, freed in `dispose()`): `particleSystem.ts` + the pure, unit-tested `particlePool.ts` draw event-driven bursts (block shards from `BLOCK_COLORS`, mob-death puffs, eat crumbs, jump/land/footstep dust) as one `THREE.Points` with a soft-sprite shader, spawned via `GameRenderer.handleEvent(event, state)` (wired into the event drain beside `audio.handleEvent`). `skyView.ts` + the pure `starField.ts` layer camera-following stars, a moon, a sun disc, and drifting canvas-noise clouds over the day-night sky lerp, ramped by `daylight`. `precipitation.ts` is the camera-following rain/snow field driven by `state.weather`, and `syncDayNight` adds the matching overcast sky tint + dimmed light + nearer fog.
101:- `audioDirector.ts` — the shell-side observer, exactly parallel to the renderer: `handleEvent(GameEvent)` plays one-shots (block break/place by material, hurt/eat/jump/land, mob attacks, death/respawn stingers) and `sync(state, dt)` drives everything continuous (footsteps, mining hit ticks, mob ambience, music mood, and the weather rain bed). Music follows `state.daylight` immediately and the biome with 5 s hysteresis, and ducks while paused. The rain bed (`rainLoop.ts`) is a looping filtered-noise source on the graph, off the SFX voice budget, whose gain tracks `state.weather` rain intensity (silent for snow / while paused). The engine never imports this module.
130:- `generation.ts` — `generateWorld(world)`: deterministic terrain, caves, lava, water, ores, trees, houses, and underground dungeons (`placeDungeons`, last in the pipeline). `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` (so it can't shift ore RNG) and before `placeDungeons` (so rooms overwrite lava). `collectDungeonSites(world)` re-derives dungeon chest/spawner indices from the seed for the engine. Constants live in the frozen `GEN` object. **Byte-identical output per seed is a save-format contract**, pinned by `generation.test.ts` hash tests — fix code, never hashes.

Weather windows and the daylight curve moved to the same portable primitives (both transient/derived — no save impact).

+- **0.12.0 (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10)** — the **aquatic update**. Kelp/coral (`BlockId`s **appended**: 55–57), sunken **shipwrecks**, and **buried treasure** all write generated blocks, so the worldgen baseline bumps 9→10 (old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed; the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md). - **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.

- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). This is the first mob persistence in the format: `isPersistentMob` keeps only **tamed pets** here (PR-B adds village residents), since the fungible population is re-created each boot. Restored before `spawnInitialMobs`, with `y` re-grounded onto the current surface and fresh ids assigned. The new `faction`/`owner`/`sitting`/`targetId`/`retargetTimer` mob fields are session-side; only the durable ones land in `SavedMob`. The wolf and cat are additive `MobKind`s with no `BlockId`/item changes, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.

+- `useMinecraftGame` creates the `GameEngine` in the canvas mount's callback ref, then an effect builds the `GameRenderer`, the `AudioDirector`, and `inputController` and drives the `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `engine.step(dt, input)` (in bounded catch-up substeps of ≤50 ms via `createAccumulator` from `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`, so slow frames — e.g. software GL — don't run the simulation in slow motion) → drain engine events (death/respawn handling, `attackSwung` → `renderer.triggerSwing()`, + `renderer.handleEvent` for particle bursts, + `audio.handleEvent`) → `minimap.sync(state)` → `renderer.sync(state)` → `audio.sync(state, dt)` → `renderer.render()`. The minimap must sync **before** the renderer because it reads `state.worldMeshDirty`, which `renderer.sync` clears.

- `components/GameShell.tsx` is the menu shell **above** `useMinecraftGame`: a profile-select → world-select → play state machine (profiles own worlds; see [save-format.md](save-format.md)) that runs the one-time legacy migration on mount and renders `MinecraftGame` keyed by `world.id` (+ a reload nonce). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset changes the key, so React unmounts the game subtree — running the effect cleanup that disposes renderer/audio/input and clears the rAF + autosave — and a fresh mount boots the next world, **no page reload**. The tab's active world is remembered in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes it while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. `useMinecraftGame` therefore takes the `world` + `profile` to play and persists to that world's own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key.

- UI state arrives as immutable `GameSnapshot`s via `useSyncExternalStore`; the engine replaces the snapshot object only when a visible value changes, so React re-renders are minimal and identity-driven.

- UI intents (`craft`, `swapSlots`, `selectSlot`, …) are dispatched as engine `Command`s. The only React state in the shell is pure UI concern: pointer lock, transient save messages, renderer failure.

## Input (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`)

Owns every DOM listener. Continuous input (movement keys, mouse button, pointer lock, CapsLock) is exposed as a `FrameInput` the engine reads each step; discrete actions (hotbar, inventory toggle, place, eat, attack, unstuck, pause, F3 debug, V camera view) become commands; mouse-look calls `engine.applyLook`. The first click only acquires pointer lock; `KeyI` exits it.

**Pause ↔ pointer lock**: the browser consumes Escape to exit pointer lock, so Esc never reaches keydown while locked — losing the lock during plain gameplay is the pause trigger (`pointerlockchange` dispatches `pause`). The inventory (`KeyI`) and death paths set their state flags _before_ the async `pointerlockchange` fires, and the engine's `pause` command additionally ignores those states, so they don't open the menu. While unlocked, Escape toggles pause directly (and closes the inventory). "Back to Game" resumes and re-requests the lock; Chrome's ~1.25 s cooldown after Esc can reject that request — the rejection is swallowed and the player just clicks the canvas.

## Inventory and items (`lib/game/`)

- `inventory.ts` — pure slot algebra (`adjustSlotCount`, `craft`, durability, armor); every function returns a new array or `null` for "no change". Crafting refuses when the result doesn't fit rather than destroying overflow. Equipped armor is **dedicated storage**: `state.equippedArmor` (`Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot | null>`) holds the worn pieces themselves — `toggleEquipArmor`/`unequipArmor` move a piece between the inventory and the record, and `equippedDefense`/`armorReduction`/`consumeEquippedArmorDurability` (and Mending's `mendXp`) read/wear/repair those instances directly rather than re-finding them in the inventory by id.

Unit-tested with a fake clock (catch-up, debt-drop cap, no drift under chronically-late callbacks).

- **Portable worldgen noise** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` **10→11**, save schema stays v16): all seed-determined noise — terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, underground speckle/flora hashes, weather windows, the daylight curve — moved from engine-defined `Math.sin` to bit-portable implementations (`lib/world/noise.ts`), so the same seed now generates **byte-identical worlds on every JS engine**. This is the groundwork for online multiplayer (a Bun server and browser clients must agree on the generated baseline to sync worlds as seed + block diff) and retires the fragile "worldgen hashes are only valid on the pinned Bun" caveat. Terrain is visually unchanged (same formulas; every structural probe passed the re-baseline untouched), but exact bytes shift: **existing worlds reboot from their seed and discard block edits**, per the standard worldgen-bump policy. Digests re-baselined into the new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`; a new Playwright spec (`e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`) proves Chromium/V8 regenerates the exact Bun/JSC baseline.

must not read them (they'd act on 'whoever is primary', which is wrong
on a server) — systems convert to explicit PlayerState params in the
next slices, after which a lint guard enforces it.

content.subject: Phase 1: Deterministic foundations (portable worldgen, TickDriver, input intents)
content.description: Branch mp/1-deterministic-foundations: new lib/world/noise.ts (portable hash/value-noise/trig), swap into generation.ts + dayNight/weather, WORLDGEN_VERSION 10→11 with hash re-baseline into lib/world/generationBaselines.ts, e2e/determinism.e2e.ts, lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts extraction, FrameInput→move intents refactor, docs (architecture/testing/save-format) + CHANGELOG. Full verify gate + e2e green.

content.subject: Phase 2: Multi-player engine core (players map, save v17)
content.description: Branch mp/2-multiplayer-engine: PlayerState absorbs ~25 flat fields, players: Map + primaryPlayerId + compat aliases (lib/game/engine/players.ts), dispatch/setPlayerInput/addPlayer/removePlayer/apiFor, authority+headless options, per-player events, all 23 systems converted in dependency order, save v17 migration, GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts, docs. Acceptance bar: entire existing e2e suite passes unchanged.

content.subject: Phase 3: Accounts, Postgres, cloud saves, invites
content.description: Branch mp/3-accounts-cloud-saves: Drizzle + postgres + PGlite tests, db/ schema (better-auth tables, worlds, worldMembers, worldInvites), better-auth server/client with anonymous plugin (integration-test guest→upgrade re-parenting FIRST), API routes (worlds CRUD, save LWW, invites, HS256 ticket mint in lib/net/tickets.ts), AccountPanel, cloudSaves sync, .env.example + docker-compose, docs/online.md.

content.subject: Phase 4: Game server + protocol v1 on Fly
content.description: Branch mp/4-game-server-protocol: lib/net/protocol.ts (v1 message unions + validators), codec (gzip), clock (RTT EWMA); server/ (index Bun.serve /health /rooms /ws, roomRegistry, room with fixed ticker + 60s persist + idle evict + backpressure, connection FSM, persistence drizzle+memory, remoteMotion applyRemotePoses with speed clamps/forcePose), Dockerfile oven/bun:1.3.12, fly.toml; ESLint no-restricted-imports for server/**; room tests with fake sockets; scripts/netProbe.ts; docs/protocol.md.

content.subject: Phase 5: Client online play (NetworkSession, avatars, chat)
content.description: Branch mp/5-client-online-play: lib/game/session.ts (GameSession seam, createLocalSession), lib/net/NetworkSession.ts (replica engine, command routing, event replay, interpolation @ serverTime−125ms, SYSTEM_SCHEDULE table), remotePlayerVisuals, Online world-select section + app/join/[token], ChatPanel + ConnectionStatus, MP pause semantics, e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts (two contexts, PERSISTENCE=memory server), manual.md.

content.subject: Phase 6: Hardening + ops (reconnect, replay, soak) → v0.13.0
content.description: Branch mp/6-hardening-ops: reconnect ladder + resync e2e, latency sim knob, per-room command log + /rooms/:id/log + server/scripts/replay.ts, owner kick + invite revocation, loadSim soak script + MAX_ROOMS tuning, /rooms stats, runbook in docs/online.md, tuning.md net constants, CHANGELOG v0.13.0.

/**
 * Migrates a v15 save to v16 — a pure version bump. `vehicles` is optional, so
 * older saves load with no placed rafts/ships.
 */
export function migrateSaveV15toV16(save: SaveDataV15): SaveDataV16 {
  return { ...save, version: 16 };
}

/**
 * Migrates a v16 save to v17: the flat single-player fields wrap into
 * `players: [{ id: "local", … }]` (a pure field move — the same values under
 * the same names, with `player` renamed to `position`), and legacy pet owners
 * (the literal "player") rewrite to the local player's id.
 */
export function migrateSaveV16toV17(save: SaveDataV16): SaveData {
  const {
    gameMode,
    gameOver,
    inventorySlots,
    equippedArmor,
    selectedSlot,
    player,
    hearts,
    hunger,
    spawnPoint,
    effects,
    xp,
    stats,
    advancements,
    mobs,
    ...world
  } = save;
  return {
    ...world,
    version: 17,
    mobs: mobs?.map((mob) => (mob.owner === "player" ? { ...mob, owner: "local" } : mob)),
    players: [
      {
        id: "local",
        position: player,
        inventorySlots,
        equippedArmor,
        selectedSlot,
        gameMode,
        gameOver,
        hearts,
        hunger,
        effects,
        xp,
        stats,
        advancements,
        spawnPoint
      }
    ]
  };
}

## What changed (read these to confirm): lib/game/types.ts (SavedPlayer + SaveDataV16 + SaveData v17), lib/game/save.ts (migrateSaveV16toV17, readSave chain now ends at 17, per-player validators retargeted), lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts serialize()/serializePlayer.

Semantics:
- `SaveData` (v17) = world-level fields (seed, worldType, difficulty, hardcore, changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dayClock, villagesSeeded) + `players: SavedPlayer[]`.
- `SavedPlayer` = { id, position?, inventorySlots?, equippedArmor?, selectedSlot?, gameMode?, gameOver?, hearts?, hunger?, effects?, xp?, stats?, advancements?, spawnPoint? } — the old flat per-player fields under the SAME names, except the old top-level `player` {x,y,z} is now `position`.
- `migrateSaveV16toV17(v16save)` wraps the flat fields into players: [{id:"local", …}] and rewrites SavedMob owner literal "player" → "local". SavedMob.owner is now any non-empty string id.
- Per-player validators now take a SavedPlayer (param still named `save`): restoreInventorySlots, restoreEquippedArmor, restoreSelectedSlot, restoreHearts, restoreHungerLevel, restoreXp, restoreGameMode, restoreSpawnPoint, restorePlayerPosition (reads .position), restoreEffects, restoreStats, restoreAdvancements.
- `restoreGameOver(save, savedPlayer)` now takes TWO args: (Pick<SaveData,"hardcore">, SavedPlayer) — true only when save.hardcore && savedPlayer.gameOver.
- World-level validators unchanged (still take SaveData): restoreDayClock, restoreDifficulty, restoreHardcore, readContainers, readLootedChests, restoreMobs, restoreVehicles. restoreMobs now accepts any non-empty-string owner for pets ("ally" faction) — a pre-v17 fixture with owner:"player" still validates, but post-migration saves carry "local".
- GameEngine.serialize() now emits version 17 with players[]; the local player's entry has id "local".

## Conversion rules for the tests
1. Round-trip tests that build a full flat SaveData literal (version: 16 or older) and feed readSave/writeSave: keep the literal as the OLD shape (typed `as unknown as` or as SaveDataV16/older versioned types — the versioned types still exist), write it to the fake storage, readSave migrates → assert on the MIGRATED v17 shape: per-player values live in `result.players[0]` (id "local", position instead of player). Assert `version === 17` where they asserted 16.
2. Direct validator-call tests (restoreHearts({hearts: …} …)): change the fixture to a SavedPlayer-shaped object (usually just add `id: "local"` or cast the minimal literal `as SavedPlayer` / adjust field name player→position). Keep each test's intent identical — they pin validation/clamping behavior, not shapes.
3. restoreGameOver call sites: pass ({hardcore: …}, {id:"local", gameOver: …}) style args matching the new signature.
4. Tests asserting serialize() output (GameEngine.test.ts / hardcore.test.ts): read the per-player fields from `save.players[0]` and expect version 17. e2e/smoke.e2e.ts has one assertion `version === 16` (grep for it) → 17; if it reads other flat save fields, follow the same players[0] mapping.
5. ADD new migration tests in save.test.ts (follow the style of the existing migrateSaveV15toV16 tests): (a) a flat v16 save migrates to players:[{id:"local",…}] with every field carried over and player→position renamed; (b) a v16 save with a pet mob owner:"player" migrates to owner:"local"; (c) readSave on a stored v15 (or earlier) save chains all the way to 17; (d) a v17 save missing `players` array → readSave returns null.
6. Do not weaken any assertion; if a test's premise no longer exists (e.g. it asserted a flat field on the serialized save), assert the equivalent on players[0].

Do NOT run e2e (just make the smoke.e2e.ts edit). Do NOT commit. Note: other engine source files are being edited concurrently — if `bun test` shows failures in files you don't own, ignore them and report; only your four files must be clean.

Return: a summary of what you changed per file, the new migration tests added, and the final test/typecheck status for your files.

- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command)`, advances `step(dt, input)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`) and the world size is overridable for fast headless tests.

input.new_string:
- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command, playerId?)` (the id says whose intent it is; the SP shell omits it), advances `step(dt, input?)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`), the world size is overridable for fast headless tests, and two options shape multiplayer hosting: `authority` ("local" honors `pause` and freezes the world while the primary player is dead — the single-player feel; "server" ignores pause and never freezes a shared world) and `headless` (skips snapshot building — a server room has no React shell). `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` are the server join/leave surface (join restores the player's persisted v17 slice; leave serializes it back for the world save); `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` stores each client's latest intent packet.
- `state.ts` — `GameState` holds the **players map** (`players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; single-player is the one-entry case) beside the world: mobs, vehicles, and thrown spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, containers, world timers. `PlayerState` owns everything per-player: avatar pose, inventory/armor/hotbar, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player UI flags, per-player timers, live input. Plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
- `players.ts` — the alias layer and player queries. The flat legacy fields (`state.player`, `state.inventory`, `state.hearts`, …) are **accessor properties delegating to the primary player**, kept permanently for the SP shell, tests, and `window.__monecraft` — but **engine systems must never read them** (they'd act on "whoever is primary", wrong on a server); an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` guard enforces this under `systems/`. Systems take the acting `PlayerState` explicitly; `nearestPlayerTo`/`nearestTargetablePlayer` are the proximity/hunt queries (mobs hunt the nearest `mobsThreaten` player and anchor flee/follow on the nearest of any mode), and `allEligiblePlayersSleeping` gates the night skip (every non-dead, non-spectator player in bed; the `wakeUp` command climbs out before the fade commits).
