content.text:
**Phase 2 is complete.** The engine is now genuinely multi-player: `feat/online-multiplayer` holds 13 commits (~2,800 insertions across 71 files), with the full verify gate and all 19 e2e specs green at every slice — single-player behaves exactly as before, which was the phase's acceptance bar.

What the engine can now do that it couldn't this morning:

- **N players in one world** — `GameState.players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`, with single-player as the one-entry case. The old flat fields (`state.player`, `state.inventory`, …) live on as accessor aliases for the shell/tests/console, and an ESLint guard bans them inside engine systems so the conversion can't regress.
- **Every system addresses players explicitly** — mobs hunt the nearest targetable player and anchor flee/pet-follow on the nearest of any mode; arrows and explosions hit whoever is actually in range; spawn waves center on a random party member with a party-scaled hostile cap; the night skips only when *everyone* eligible is in bed (new `wakeUp` command to back out).
- **The server surface exists** — `dispatch(command, playerId)` and `applyLook(…, playerId)` attribute intents to the commanding player; `setPlayerInput` stores per-client intent packets; `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` restore/serialize a player's slice on join/leave; `authority: "server"` ignores pause and never freezes the shared world; `headless` skips snapshot work.
- **Save v17** — per-player slices in a `players` array; old saves migrate automatically; pet owners become real player ids. Nine new multiplayer tests pin all of this (1,018 tests total).

One session note: the subagent I delegated test fixups to hit its session limit mid-run, but it had already completed ~95% of the work; I verified and finished the remainder myself.

**Next per plan is Phase 3** — the Vercel side: Postgres/Drizzle schema, better-auth with anonymous guest→upgrade (integration-testing the "guest keeps worlds" re-parenting first), the worlds/invites/save/ticket API routes, and cloud-save sync. That phase adds the first new dependencies (`better-auth`, `drizzle-orm`, `postgres`, PGlite for tests) and needs env/database setup, so it's a natural checkpoint if you'd like to review the branch so far — otherwise I'll proceed.

Online co-op multiplayer, delivered in phases on this one branch (per the agreed plan). Draft while the remaining phases land; each phase keeps the full verify gate + Playwright suite green.

## Architecture (decided up front)

- **Scale:** 2–8 player private co-op worlds, invite links; full-world rooms (no chunk streaming in v1).
- **Hosting:** Vercel (Next.js app, better-auth, world/save/invite API, Neon Postgres) + Fly.io (one Bun process hosting world rooms — one authoritative `GameEngine` each at 20 Hz over WebSocket). Portable Docker container; the two share only Neon and a ticket-signing secret.
- **Authority:** server-authoritative world (every gameplay command validated and executed server-side); each client owns only its own avatar movement (streamed, server-clamped). Wire format leaves room for full server-auth + prediction later.
- **Auth:** better-auth with anonymous sessions — instant guest play, in-place upgrade to a real account keeping worlds.
- **Single-player is unchanged:** fully offline, localStorage saves, same engine (the one-player case), no account needed.

## Landed

### Phase 1 — deterministic foundations
- **Portable worldgen** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11): all seed-determined noise moved to bit-portable implementations (`lib/world/noise.ts`) — same formulas on a polynomial sine, integer hashes. The same seed now generates **byte-identical worlds on every JS engine**; `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves Chromium ≡ the Bun baseline (the property seed+diff world sync rests on). Existing worlds re-roll from their seed per the standard worldgen-bump policy; every structural probe passed the re-baseline untouched. Retires the "hashes only valid on pinned Bun" caveat.
- **Tick drivers**: the rAF catch-up accumulator extracted to `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`, plus the drift-corrected fixed 20 Hz ticker the server will use.
- **Input intents**: `FrameInput` carries abstract movement intents; DOM key codes, CapsLock, and pointer lock now live only in the input controller.

### Phase 2 — multi-player engine core (save v16→v17)
- `GameState.players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; the old flat fields remain as accessor aliases onto the primary player for the shell/tests/`window.__monecraft`, with an ESLint guard banning them inside engine systems.
- All 23 systems take the acting player: mobs hunt the nearest targetable player; arrows/explosions hit whoever is in range; spawn waves center on a random party member with a party-scaled cap; night skips only when every eligible player sleeps (new `wakeUp` command).

- **Save v17**: per-player slices in a `players` array; automatic migration; pet owners become real player ids. 9-test multiplayer suite pins the semantics.
- Acceptance bar held: **single-player behavior unchanged — the entire pre-existing e2e suite passes as-is.**

- **Phase 3** — accounts, Postgres (Drizzle), cloud saves, invites, join tickets (Vercel side)

- **Phase 5** — client online play (NetworkSession + replica engine, remote avatars, chat, invite links)
- **Phase 6** — hardening/ops (reconnect, latency sim, command-log replay, soak) → v0.13.0

Per slice: `bun run lint` · `bun run typecheck` · `bun run format:check` · `bun test` (1,018 tests) · `bun run build`, plus the full Playwright suite (19 specs incl. the new cross-engine determinism spec) at each behavior-touching slice. import { PGlite } from "@electric-sql/pglite";
import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/pglite";
import * as schema from "./schema";

/**
 * An in-memory Postgres (PGlite/WASM) with the full schema applied — bun test
 * exercises real SQL against the real drizzle schema with no daemon. Not a
 * .test.ts file: it's a fixture imported by tests (and by the game server's
 * PERSISTENCE=memory mode later).
 *
 * The DDL mirrors db/schema.ts. drizzle-kit generates the production
 * migrations from the same schema module, and the auth integration test
 * exercises every table, so drift between this DDL and schema.ts fails fast.
 */
export async function createTestDb() {
  const client = new PGlite();
  await client.exec(`
    CREATE TABLE "user" (
      id text PRIMARY KEY,
      name text NOT NULL,
      email text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      email_verified boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      image text,
      created_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      updated_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      is_anonymous boolean,
      skin_id text
    );
    CREATE TABLE "session" (
      id text PRIMARY KEY,
      expires_at timestamp NOT NULL,
      token text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      created_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      updated_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      ip_address text,
      user_agent text,
      user_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    );
    CREATE TABLE "account" (
      id text PRIMARY KEY,
      account_id text NOT NULL,
      provider_id text NOT NULL,
      user_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      access_token text,
      refresh_token text,
      id_token text,
      access_token_expires_at timestamp,
      refresh_token_expires_at timestamp,
      scope text,
      password text,
      created_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      updated_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );
    CREATE TABLE "verification" (
      id text PRIMARY KEY,
      identifier text NOT NULL,
      value text NOT NULL,
      expires_at timestamp NOT NULL,
      created_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      updated_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );
    CREATE TABLE worlds (
      id text PRIMARY KEY,
      owner_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      kind text NOT NULL,
      name text NOT NULL,
      seed integer NOT NULL,
      world_type text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',
      game_mode text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'survival',
      difficulty text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal',
      hardcore boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      worldgen_version integer NOT NULL,
      save_version integer,
      save_blob bytea,
      created_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      updated_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );
    CREATE TABLE world_members (
      world_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES worlds(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      user_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      role text NOT NULL,
      joined_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX world_members_pk ON world_members (world_id, user_id);
    CREATE TABLE world_invites (
      id text PRIMARY KEY,
      world_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES worlds(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      token text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      created_by text NOT NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      expires_at timestamp,
      max_uses integer,
      uses integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
      created_at timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );
  `);
  return drizzle(client, { schema });
}

export type TestDb = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createTestDb>>;

Auth is better-auth with the anonymous plugin: a guest identity on the

memberships, and invites onto the new account before the anonymous user

the real better-auth flow and real SQL, including the collision case

duplicate folds away via the unique index). Tested FIRST per the plan:
this hook is what 'guests keep their worlds' hangs on.

lib/net/tickets.ts is the only trust link between the two deployments:
the Next API mints a 60s HS256 ticket (Web Crypto, no jwt dependency)
naming player/world/role/protocol; the game server verifies it with the
shared secret and never touches cookies. Verification is total on
hostile input (tamper/expiry/garbage tests).

Deps: better-auth, drizzle-orm, postgres; drizzle-kit + PGlite (dev)." && git log --oneline -1

# Online: accounts, cloud saves, multiplayer

How the online stack fits together, and how to run it. The offline
single-player game needs **none** of this: without an online action, the
client never makes an auth request (the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage
flag gates even the session check).

## The pieces

```
Browser ──(cookies)── Next.js app          ── Neon/Postgres
   │                   /api/auth/*   better-auth (guests + accounts)
   │                   /api/worlds…  world CRUD, invites, cloud saves
   │                   /api/worlds/:id/ticket   mints 60s HS256 join ticket
   │
   └──(ws + ticket)── Game server (Bun, Fly.io)  ── same Postgres
                       one authoritative GameEngine room per world (phase 4)
```

The web app and the game server never talk to each other at runtime: the
join ticket (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, signed with the shared
`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`) is the only trust link, and both read the same
Postgres.

## Identity: guests first

- "Play online as guest" (menu → Account panel) creates a real better-auth
  user with `isAnonymous` — no form, instant play. Guests own worlds and
  memberships like anyone else.
- Upgrading (sign-up, or sign-in to an existing account, while holding the
  guest session) triggers the anonymous plugin's `onLinkAccount` hook
  (`lib/auth/server.ts`): worlds, memberships, and invites re-parent onto the
  new account before the guest row is deleted. **This hook is the "guests
  keep their worlds" promise** — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts` proves it against
  the real better-auth flow on real SQL (PGlite), including the
  duplicate-membership collision case.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves

`lib/online/worldsService.ts` owns the rules (membership-gated reads that
present as `not-found` so ids can't be probed; owner-gated rename/delete/
invite; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses). The `app/api`
routes are thin HTTP adapters over it.

Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the client pulls the newer
save before retrying. Wiring the sync into the world list / autosave path
lands together with the multiplayer world browser in the online shell phase.

## Environment & local development

See `.env.example` for every variable (web: `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`; game server adds `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`,
`ADMIN_TOKEN`).

```bash
docker compose up -d          # local Postgres (dev only — tests use PGlite)
bunx drizzle-kit migrate      # apply db/migrations once
bun run dev                   # web app with accounts + API
```

Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.

## Production

- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
- **Fly.io** (game server, phase 4): shares `DATABASE_URL` and
  `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` with the web app.

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	Guidance for AI coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, …) working in this repository. This file is the single source of truth — CLAUDE.md imports it.
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	A Minecraft-inspired voxel game: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, Bun. Single-player, browser-based, client-only, saves to localStorage.
8	
9	**Zero binary assets**: every asset is generated at runtime — textures and sprites from pixel code, sound and music synthesized via ZZFX/WebAudio. New content should follow this principle unless the user decides otherwise. The one sanctioned exception is the UI pixel font (Monocraft, a Minecraft-style face under the SIL OFL 1.1), self-hosted via `next/font/local` from the committed woff2 in `app/fonts/` — don't "fix" it back to a system font.
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash
14	bun install        # Install dependencies
15	bun run dev        # Dev server at http://localhost:3000
16	bun run build      # Production build — part of the verification baseline
17	bun run lint       # ESLint (flat config, eslint .)
18	bun run typecheck  # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
19	bun run format     # Prettier --write (CI runs format:check — unformatted files fail the build)
20	bun test           # Unit + integration + component tests
21	bun run test:e2e   # Playwright browser smoke tests (needs `bunx playwright install chromium` once)
22	```
23	
24	## Development Workflow
25	
26	For a non-trivial change:
27	
28	- **Branch only for big work.** A new feature, a large refactor or improvement, a dependency upgrade, or broad/risky work spanning many systems gets its own `<type>/<topic>` branch off `main` (e.g. `upgrade/next16-react19-three184`) so it lands as one reviewable unit. Minor work — bug fixes, small improvements, doc edits, single-purpose tweaks — commits straight to `main`, even when it touches a few files. Judge by scope and risk, not file count; when unsure, prefer `main`. Either way, the verify gate below must be green before anything lands on `main`.
29	- **Commit in focused slices.** One commit per logical slice (e.g. split a dead-code removal from the feature that replaces it). Keep `bun run lint` green at each commit so the branch stays bisectable. Use Conventional Commit messages; no `Co-Authored-By` trailers.
30	- **Explain the why in the commit body.** The subject says what changed; the body (separated by a blank line) explains why — the problem or motivation, and any non-obvious decision or trade-off. A body is required for anything beyond trivial edits (typos, formatting); `git log` should make sense without opening the PR.
31	- **Docs and tests ship _with_ the change — not later.** A change isn't done until the docs match it: the **Docs** section below says what each `docs/` file tracks, so update every page that covers what you touched — a `config.ts` tunable, a system, a mechanic, content, the save format — **not just the obviously behavioral ones** (a new tunable or a new test almost always has a companion doc that needs the same edit). Cover new logic with tests, keep the test coverage map current, and add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Flag any save-format or worldgen impact.
32	- **Verify before it lands** (before opening a PR, or before committing minor work straight to `main`): `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, and `bun run build` green (the same list CI's `verify` job runs); `bun run test:e2e` for changes touching the renderer, input, or React shell. A manual gameplay pass is only needed for pointer-lock handling or visual-appearance changes (see docs/testing.md). Then confirm the docs, tests, and `CHANGELOG.md` cover everything you changed (see the docs bullet above) — that check is part of the gate, not an afterthought.
33	- **Open the PR against this fork's `main`** (`gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main`); do not add AI-attribution lines (e.g. "Generated with …") to the description. Pushing and opening PRs are user-authorized — don't push or open a PR unless asked.
34	
35	## Docs
36	
37	- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — engine/renderer/audio/shell layers, step order, engine invariants & gotchas
38	- [docs/adding-content.md](docs/adding-content.md) — step-by-step: new block / item / recipe / mob / mechanic
39	- [docs/save-format.md](docs/save-format.md) — save schema, autosave, compatibility rules
40	- [docs/online.md](docs/online.md) — accounts/guests, cloud saves, invites, join tickets, env setup, local online dev
41	- [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) — test coverage map and the worldgen hash re-baseline policy
42	- [docs/tuning.md](docs/tuning.md) — gameplay tunables in `config.ts`, grouped by effect with balance trade-offs
43	- [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md) — player guide (gameplay, survival, crafting, mobs, farming)
44	- [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md) — gameplay reference tables (recipes, blocks, mobs, items)
45	- `README.md` — player-facing controls and quick start

1	# Architecture
2	
3	Three layers with hard boundaries:
4	
5	```
6	React UI (components/)          declarative HUD/panels; reads snapshots, sends commands
7	    │  useSyncExternalStore + engine commands
8	GameEngine (lib/game/engine/)   headless simulation: all game state, stepped per frame
9	    │  reads/writes
10	Voxel world (lib/world/)        data + generation + meshing + queries
11	    ▲  read every frame by
12	GameRenderer (lib/game/render/) Three.js: maps simulation state → GPU objects
13	AudioDirector (lib/game/audio/)  WebAudio: maps engine events + state → procedural sound
14	```
15	
16	The engine has **no React, no DOM, no rendering** — it runs (and is tested) headlessly in `bun test`. The renderer, the audio director, and the input controller are the only modules touching Three.js scene objects, the `AudioContext`, and DOM listeners respectively.
17	
18	The ONLINE layer (accounts, cloud saves, invites, join tickets) sits beside the shell: better-auth + Postgres behind `app/api` route handlers that adapt the tested rules in `lib/online/worldsService.ts` — see [online.md](online.md). Offline single-player never touches it.
19	
20	## React shell (`lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/`)
21	
22	- `useMinecraftGame` creates the `GameEngine` in the canvas mount's callback ref, then an effect builds the `GameRenderer`, the `AudioDirector`, and `inputController` and drives the `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `engine.step(dt, input)` (in bounded catch-up substeps of ≤50 ms via `createAccumulator` from `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`, so slow frames — e.g. software GL — don't run the simulation in slow motion) → drain engine events (death/respawn handling, `attackSwung` → `renderer.triggerSwing()`, + `renderer.handleEvent` for particle bursts, + `audio.handleEvent`) → `minimap.sync(state)` → `renderer.sync(state)` → `audio.sync(state, dt)` → `renderer.render()`. The minimap must sync **before** the renderer because it reads `state.worldMeshDirty`, which `renderer.sync` clears.
23	- `components/GameShell.tsx` is the menu shell **above** `useMinecraftGame`: a profile-select → world-select → play state machine (profiles own worlds; see [save-format.md](save-format.md)) that runs the one-time legacy migration on mount and renders `MinecraftGame` keyed by `world.id` (+ a reload nonce). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset changes the key, so React unmounts the game subtree — running the effect cleanup that disposes renderer/audio/input and clears the rAF + autosave — and a fresh mount boots the next world, **no page reload**. The tab's active world is remembered in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes it while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. `useMinecraftGame` therefore takes the `world` + `profile` to play and persists to that world's own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key.
24	- UI state arrives as immutable `GameSnapshot`s via `useSyncExternalStore`; the engine replaces the snapshot object only when a visible value changes, so React re-renders are minimal and identity-driven.
25	- UI intents (`craft`, `swapSlots`, `selectSlot`, …) are dispatched as engine `Command`s. The only React state in the shell is pure UI concern: pointer lock, transient save messages, renderer failure.
26	- WebGL init failure is surfaced as `rendererError` and rendered as a fallback panel instead of crashing.
27	- On mount the shell installs a `window.__monecraft` debug handle (`{ engine, renderer, input, audio }`) and deletes it on unmount. The Playwright suite in `e2e/` drives the game through this handle — asserting on engine state and `renderer.renderedTriangles()` rather than pixels (see [testing.md](testing.md)); it's also handy from the browser console.
28	- UI pixel art is procedural: `lib/ui/` generates 16×16 item/HUD sprites as pure pixel buffers (`spritePixels.ts`, `hudPixels.ts` — DOM-free, unit-tested) wrapped by a cached canvas→data-URL layer (`sprites.ts`, falls back to a transparent pixel under happy-dom). `chromeTiles.ts` (`installUiTiles`, idempotent, `document`-guarded) installs the GUI textures as CSS vars: the menu-backdrop noise (`--mc-tile-dirt/stone`) and the chrome grain layered over the flat panel/slot/button colors (`--mc-tile-panel/well/button`, which default to `none` so SSR/pre-install falls back to the solid color). No image assets, no licensing exposure. `lib/ui/` must not import Three.js or the engine.
29	- Item hovers use `useItemTooltip` (`components/game/ItemTooltip.tsx`): a cursor-following, `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events:none` tooltip portaled to `document.body` (so it never clips inside the scrollable inventory or blocks the pointer-lock click), replacing native `title=` on the hotbar, inventory, and recipe entries. Elements keep their `aria-label` for the accessible name.
30	- The one binary asset is the UI pixel font (Monocraft, a Minecraft-style face under SIL OFL 1.1), self-hosted via `next/font/local` from the committed woff2 in `app/fonts/` and exposed as `--mc-font`; the monospace stack stays as the fallback and on the F3 debug readout, and Monocraft's coding ligatures are disabled in `base.css`. This is the single sanctioned exception to "zero binary assets".
31	- Note for the React Compiler lint rules: consume the hook with destructuring (`const { … } = useMinecraftGame()`); property access on the result object can false-positive `react-hooks/refs`.
32	
33	## Game engine (`lib/game/engine/`)
34	
35	- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command, playerId?)` (the id says whose intent it is; the SP shell omits it), advances `step(dt, input?)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`), the world size is overridable for fast headless tests, and two options shape multiplayer hosting: `authority` ("local" honors `pause` and freezes the world while the primary player is dead — the single-player feel; "server" ignores pause and never freezes a shared world) and `headless` (skips snapshot building — a server room has no React shell). `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` are the server join/leave surface (join restores the player's persisted v17 slice; leave serializes it back for the world save); `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` stores each client's latest intent packet.
36	- `state.ts` — `GameState` holds the **players map** (`players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; single-player is the one-entry case) beside the world: mobs, vehicles, and thrown spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, containers, world timers. `PlayerState` owns everything per-player: avatar pose, inventory/armor/hotbar, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player UI flags, per-player timers, live input. Plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
37	- `players.ts` — the alias layer and player queries. The flat legacy fields (`state.player`, `state.inventory`, `state.hearts`, …) are **accessor properties delegating to the primary player**, kept permanently for the SP shell, tests, and `window.__monecraft` — but **engine systems must never read them** (they'd act on "whoever is primary", wrong on a server); an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` guard enforces this under `systems/`. Systems take the acting `PlayerState` explicitly; `nearestPlayerTo`/`nearestTargetablePlayer` are the proximity/hunt queries (mobs hunt the nearest `mobsThreaten` player and anchor flee/follow on the nearest of any mode), and `allEligiblePlayersSleeping` gates the night skip (every non-dead, non-spectator player in bed; the `wakeUp` command climbs out before the fade commits).
38	- `commands.ts` — the `Command` union: every UI/input mutation enters the simulation through exactly this door.
39	- `tickDriver.ts` — how wall time becomes `step(dt)` calls: `createAccumulator` (variable-dt catch-up stepping, the browser shell's driver) and `createFixedTicker` (drift-corrected fixed 20 Hz ticks, the driver for a headless authoritative server). The engine itself stays dt-agnostic; both drivers clamp runaway catch-up identically (≤5 owed steps of ≤50 ms, older debt dropped).

content.text:
**Phase 3 is complete and pushed** — PR #43 now carries 16 commits, all gates green (1,039 unit tests, 19/19 e2e).

What landed for accounts and cloud saves:

- **Guests provably keep their worlds.** This was the phase's riskiest bet, so it was tested first: the better-auth `onLinkAccount` hook re-parents worlds, memberships, and invite links onto the upgraded account, verified by integration tests running the *real* auth flow against *real* SQL (PGlite, in-memory — CI needs no database daemon). Including the nasty case where a guest and their existing account share a world membership — the duplicate folds away cleanly.
- **The worlds API**: membership-gated CRUD (outsiders get `not-found` so world ids can't be probed), owner-only rename/delete/invite, idempotent invite acceptance with expiry and max-uses, and gzipped cloud-save blobs with a last-write-wins stale guard (a second device gets a 409 and pulls the newer save instead of clobbering). All rules live in a tested service module; the route handlers are one-screen adapters.
- **Join tickets**: 60-second HS256 tokens minted by the web app and verified by the future game server with a shared secret — the only trust link between the two deployments; the game server never sees a cookie.
- **The Account panel** in the menu: "Play online as guest" (one click), sign-in, and the guest-upgrade button labeled exactly for what it does — "Keep my worlds — create account."
- **Offline-first, structurally**: until a browser uses an online feature once, the client makes *zero* auth requests — plain single-player, database-less dev servers, and the e2e suite see no traffic at all.

Two deliberate deferrals, noted in the docs: wiring cloud sync into the world list/autosave UX ships together with the Phase 5 online shell rework (the transport is ready and tested), and dev setup is `docker compose up -d` + `bunx drizzle-kit migrate` when you want to try accounts locally.

**Next: Phase 4** — the Bun game server itself: the full protocol catalog, room lifecycle with the fixed 20 Hz ticker, pose validation, Postgres persistence, and the Fly deploy config. Continuing now.

# Wire protocol (v1)

The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.

## Transport & framing

WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
contract, not the encoding.

## Handshake

1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).

A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.

## Steady state

**Client → server**
- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
  distance stats, and fall damage.
- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.

**Server → client**
- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since last
  tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob poses
  (~10 Hz), the day clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-
  authoritative delta of YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…),
  sent only on change.
- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.

Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events
and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.

## Close codes

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time) |
| 4001 | protocol version mismatch |
| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS |
| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) |
| 4004 | idle timeout |

# Wire protocol (v1)

The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.

## Transport & framing

WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
contract, not the encoding.

## Handshake

1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).

A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.

## Steady state

**Client → server**
- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
  distance stats, and fall damage.
- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.

**Server → client**
- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since last
  tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob poses
  (~10 Hz), the day clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-
  authoritative delta of YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…),
  sent only on change.
- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.

Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events
and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.

## Close codes

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time) |
| 4001 | protocol version mismatch |
| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS |
| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) |
| 4004 | idle timeout |
| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) |
| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure) |

## Trust model

The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes
in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned
thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly). The
claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for
invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side
rewind validation would need.
